b1-02-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Have You Tried Sushi?
b1-02-01.scenario: Petra asks Meg whether she has ever tried sushi. You (Meg) have already tried it, but you have never tried halászlé.
b1-02-01.prompt: Tell Petra that you have already tried sushi and that you have never tried halászlé.
cues: Say that you have already tried sushi
Say that you have never tried halászlé
b1-02-01.target: Igen, már próbáltam szusit, de még soha nem próbáltam ki a halászlét.
b1-02-01.english: Yes, I have already tried sushi, but I have never tried halászlé.
b1-02-01.canDo: I can say I've already had an experience using már + past tense.

b1-02-02.title: Communicative Challenge: My First Trip Alone
b1-02-02.scenario: Petra asks Meg about the first time she travelled alone. You (Meg) were very nervous before you set off, and it was a big challenge.
b1-02-02.prompt: Tell Petra that you travelled alone for the first time in your life and how you felt before you set off.
cues: Say that it was your first time in your life
Say how you felt before you set off
b1-02-02.target: Életemben először utaztam egyedül, és nagy kihívás volt. Mielőtt elindultam, nagyon ideges voltam.
b1-02-02.english: I travelled alone for the first time in my life, and it was a big challenge. Before I set off, I was very nervous.
b1-02-02.canDo: I can mark an event as a first-time experience using először and életemben először.

b1-02-03.title: Communicative Challenge: My Mother's Cooking
b1-02-03.scenario: Petra asks Meg which food she remembers best from home. You (Meg) love the meals your mother prepared, and your grandmother's soup made a deep impression on you.
b1-02-03.prompt: Tell Petra that you love the meals your mother prepared and that your grandmother's soup made a deep impression on you.
cues: Say that you love the meals your mother prepared
Say that your grandmother's soup made a deep impression on you
b1-02-03.target: Szeretem az anyám által elkészített ételeket. A nagymamám levese mély benyomást tett rám.
b1-02-03.english: I love the meals prepared by my mother. My grandmother's soup made a deep impression on me.
b1-02-03.canDo: I can form a past participle from a verb and use it as an adjective, like elkészített étel.

b1-02-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Looking Back
b1-02-04.scenario: Károly asks Meg how she has changed over the last years. You (Meg) were afraid of new situations before, but you have changed a lot since then.
b1-02-04.prompt: Tell Károly that looking back at the past years you have changed a lot, and what you were afraid of before.
cues: Say that you are looking back at the past years
Say that you have changed a lot
Say what you were afraid of before
b1-02-04.target: Ha visszatekintek az elmúlt évekre, sokat változtam. Azelőtt féltem az új helyzetektől.
b1-02-04.english: If I look back at the past years, I have changed a lot. Before that, I was afraid of new situations.
b1-02-04.canDo: I can frame a reflection on the past using ha visszatekintek, and say what I am looking back at with -ra/-re.

b1-02-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Trips
b1-02-05.scenario: Petra asks Meg about her trips to Japan. You (Meg) have been there before, but this was your first time without Károly; you were nervous before, and you have been getting braver since.
b1-02-05.prompt: Tell Petra that you have already been to Japan, that this was your first time without Károly, and how you have changed since then.
cues: Say that you have already been to Japan
Say that this time was the first time
Say how you have changed since then
b1-02-05.target: Már jártam Japánban, de most jártam ott először Károly nélkül. Azelőtt ideges voltam, azóta egyre bátrabb vagyok.
b1-02-05.english: I have already been to Japan, but this time I was there for the first time without Károly. Before I was nervous; since then I have been getting braver and braver.
b1-02-05.canDo: I can put experiential már/még soha, first-time framing, participle adjectives and looking-back language together in one reflection.

b1-02-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Been There, Never Eaten That
b1-02-consolidation.scenario: Károly asks Meg about the places she has visited and the foods she has eaten. You (Meg) have already been to Japan, but you have never eaten halászlé.
b1-02-consolidation.prompt: Tell Károly that you have already been to Japan and that you have never eaten halászlé.
cues: Say that you have already been to Japan
Say that you have never eaten halászlé
b1-02-consolidation.target: Már jártam Japánban, de még soha nem ettem halászlét.
b1-02-consolidation.english: I have already been to Japan, but I have never eaten halászlé.
b1-02-consolidation.canDo: I can talk about experiences using már and még soha nem with past tense.
